Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

become verb

also turn into, come to be, what will become of …?, get

classical

Cic. Fam. 16.21.7: rūsticus Rōmānus factus es
Hor. Ars 25–26: brevis esse labōrō, obscūrus fīō

fīō, fierī, factus sum

verb, irregular: the passive of faciō

become, be made

With a noun or an adjective that agrees with the subject (obscūrus fīō). Quid mē fīet? is “what will become of me?”, with the ablative of the person, the dative or dē (Lewis & Short, s.v. faciō); ut fit is “as usually happens” (Liv. 3.1.7). Many changes of state have a verb of their own in -scō: jam advesperāscit, it’s getting dark (Ter. And. 581).

Other words

  • ēvādō, ēvādere, ēvāsī, ēvāsum — turn out, end up as

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.126: quōs jūdicābat nōn posse ōrātōrēs ēvādere

    Of how someone or something turns out in the end.

Examples

  • sed quid Tulliolā meā fīet? jam id vōs vidēte; mihi deest cōnsilium.

    but what will become of my little Tullia? You must see to that now; I am at a loss.Cic. Fam. 14.4.3

  • dēpōnendae tibi sunt urbānitātēs; rūsticus Rōmānus factus es

    you must put away your town manners: you have become a Roman countrymanCic. Fam. 16.21.7

  • lēnior et melior fīs accēdente senectā?

    are you growing gentler and better as old age comes on?Hor. Ep. 2.2.211

See also make, when you’re big.
